scope.success_criterion: given a real state, contract and candidate plan, the system produces a re-checkable certification credential, and any state / contract / plan drift or hard-constraint failure is REFUSED before any write-back; it need NOT prove the real environment performed an install (that is B3)

counterexamples.name: state drift after certification (reveal)
counterexamples.construction: build a credential at event k; capture the state at event k+1 (a reveal clears the mutable tail and moves the clock); re-verify the credential against the later state
counterexamples.expected: REFUSE installation; refusal reason must name the state identity mismatch
counterexamples.must_not: install; or pass because the plan happens to hash the same
counterexamples.assertion: allow == False and 'state_hash_mismatch' in refusals and state hashes differ

counterexamples.name: contract or profile change after certification
counterexamples.construction: certify under the effective contract (v1 + o0cc-pilot-devmean-equal-v2); then re-verify with a credential whose contract_hash / effective_contract_hash / profile_hash differ (a ColdChainContractV2 and/or a different ObjectiveProfile)
counterexamples.expected: REFUSE installation; the refusal must name the contract identity mismatch
counterexamples.must_not: install; or pass because the plan is unchanged
counterexamples.constraint: ColdChainContractV2 has no manifest round-trip loader (whole-tree search, B1 survey) so the variant is built in-process
counterexamples.assertion: allow == False and ('contract_hash_mismatch' in refusals or 'effective_contract_hash_mismatch' in refusals or 'profile_hash_mismatch' in refusals)

counterexamples.name: pre/post-prepare anchor confusion
counterexamples.construction: build two credentials for the SAME decision point, one anchored post_prepare (default) and one claiming pre_prepare, then compare / validate
counterexamples.expected: the anchor mismatch is EXPLICITLY RECORDED, not silently averaged or ignored
counterexamples.must_not: accept a credential whose declared anchor disagrees with the state it was built from
counterexamples.assertion: the credential carries state_capture_anchor; verifying a credential whose anchor differs from the required anchor is refused with 'anchor_mismatch', and the two anchors' state hashes are recorded as different

counterexamples.name: plan identity blind spot: anchor_time changes, legacy plan hash does not
counterexamples.construction: two plans identical in (vehicle key, anchor_node, suffix) but differing in anchor_time and/or anchor_load
counterexamples.expected: the STRONG plan identity detects the change
counterexamples.assertion: plan_hash_legacy equal AND plan_digest_anchor_v1 differs AND credential validation reports 'plan_digest_anchor_mismatch' when the two are compared

counterexamples.name: time-window or capacity violation
counterexamples.construction: feed the composed certifier a plan that violates a time window (arrival after tw_end) and one that violates capacity
counterexamples.must_not: the energy check masking the TW/capacity failures (certify_plan does not check them)
counterexamples.assertion: ok == False and the route_feasible component reports the specific failure reason ('tw' / 'capacity')

counterexamples.name: C0 energy budget exceeded
counterexamples.construction: feed a plan whose completion energy exceeds B (B set below the certified value) and one that fits
counterexamples.expected: the composed certification REFUSES on the energy component
counterexamples.must_not: pass on the grounds that TW/capacity are fine
counterexamples.assertion: ok == False with the energy component reporting feasible=False, and a control run with a sufficient B passing that component

counterexamples.name: commitment / ownership / protected violation
counterexamples.construction: three separate injections: (a) a plan that re-plans a committed customer, (b) a plan whose partition misses or duplicates a customer, (c) a plan that changes a protected vehicle
counterexamples.must_not: any of the three being absorbed by another component
counterexamples.assertion: ok == False for each, with the responsible component named (repair_plan / full_partition)

counterexamples.name: quality / fish-salability hard constraint
counterexamples.construction: run the composed certifier where the decision-time quality answer is unknown, and separately inject an explicit decision-time quality check that fails
counterexamples.expected: (a) with no executable online check: the certification result must MARK THE CAPABILITY GAP and refuse installability -- it must NOT default to pass; (b) with an injected check that fails: REFUSE
counterexamples.must_not: reporting 'all four functions were called therefore the cold-chain hard constraints are covered'
counterexamples.evidence: certify_route leaves projected_energy_kwh / projected_quality_loss / projected_thermal_margin as None (action_contract.py:171-173) and the only salability check is terminal (coldchain_evaluator_a1.py:115-117)
counterexamples.assertion: capability_gaps['quality_salability'] == 'CAPABILITY_GAP_BLOCKING' and installable == False in case (a); ok == False in case (b)

counterexamples.name: state identity must not import future information
counterexamples.construction: audit the state identity's inputs: classify every snapshot key; verify visible_mask equals exactly {c : reveal_time[c] <= clock}; verify every customer in every plan suffix is visible; then mutate a copy of the snapshot and require the expected sensitivities
counterexamples.expected: the identity depends only on decision-time state, the already-revealed set and the contract identity; no unrevealed customer's attribute enters it
counterexamples.must_not: reading future order attributes merely to compute the hash
counterexamples.assertion: state_identity_information_scope records the classification; unrevealed_customers_contributing == []; flipping visible_mask of an unrevealed customer in a COPY changes the hash (so the visible set is bound); and no snapshot key holds reveal_time/demands/tw/quality arrays

additional_invariants.identity_matching_is_not_sufficient: the three identity equalities do NOT replace the deadline check, the completeness of certification, or the actual install-result check (the last belongs to B3); a credential whose identities all match but whose certification is incomplete or whose deadline was missed must still be refused
